name: OneRepublic
notes: The "sad piano anthem" template, written here as an *artist* only — the volume assigns Ryan Tedder's producer entry to `pop-2020s`, so this model covers the band's 2006–2009 records and nothing else. 76–120 straight, backbeat on 2&4. Harmony is a single minor four-chord loop "through every section (i–VI–III–VII); the lift is dynamic, not harmonic; no modulation", so one family dominates and the arrangement carries the dynamic instead. Three drum deltas are quoted: "kick 1 and 3", "snare/clap on the backbeat entering **only at the chorus**" (a low ghost probability and a `dropOutBeats` of 0.9, which is how a late-entering backbeat reads to the generator), and "16th shaker", which leads the perc block; the remix that became the radio version "adds an extra percussion line and samples", which is why the percussion density is higher than the kit's. The low end is "cello and bass guitar covering the low end… long notes on roots" — `mirror_kick` at 0.95. The melody is "a descending stepwise phrase repeated with rising intensity", i.e. a high step share with a descend-dominant contour, and the viola/cello lines answer as the counter. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research says so and marks the key/BPM **[LOW-CONF]** — there is no published key or tempo for the signature single, so `bpm.mode` 92 is this author's centre of the stated band. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are all drum probabilities. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“cello and bass guitar covering the low end (the band's cellist doubles on bass), long notes on roots.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
